title: Midpoint flight time
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the time of flight for the particle hitting the midpoint of AB, using the vertical displacement of 1.5h and the kinematic equation.

title: Velocity range endpoints
description: Essential: Correctly identifies the initial velocities for particles hitting points A and B as the limits of the detectable range.

title: Energy conservation application
description: Important: Applies conservation of energy correctly to equate total mechanical energy for particles hitting A and B, given their speeds are equal.

title: Kinematic setup for limits
description: Important: Uses projectile motion equations (vertical displacement and constant horizontal velocity) to find the times of flight and initial velocities for the extreme points A and B.

title: Final L-h relationship
description: Essential: Derives and states the final numerical relationship between L and h from the energy equation.

title: Correct vertical displacements
description: Important: Identifies the correct vertical displacements from P to A (h) and P to B (2h) for use in the kinematic equations.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Maintains consistent units throughout the derivation or explicitly includes them in final answers.

title: Sign or displacement error
description: Pitfall: Uses an incorrect vertical displacement (e.g., 0.5h for the midpoint, or confuses heights for A and B) in the kinematic equations.

title: Energy equation error
description: Pitfall: Makes an error in setting up the conservation of energy equation, such as incorrect gravitational potential energy terms for points A or B.
